chief_complaint: Post‑myocardial infarction follow‑up and chronic disease management
history_of_present_illness: The patient is a 44‑year‑old male with a recent acute NSTEMI (April 2022) and a history of myocardial infarction. Since then he has been managed on secondary‑prevention therapy including aspirin, a beta‑blocker, and statins. He has longstanding essential hypertension (diagnosed 2003) now classified as stage 1, hyperlipidemia diagnosed 2023, and type 2 diabetes mellitus with micro‑albuminuria indicating early diabetic nephropathy. Chronic kidney disease progressed to stage 2 in 2023, with prior stage 1 disease and diabetic kidney disorder documented. Over the past year he has experienced significant psychosocial stressors: social isolation, limited social contact, and intimate‑partner abuse, as well as recent dental problems leading to loss of teeth. He is employed full‑time and has a criminal record. Recent labs show good glycemic control (A1c 5.2%) but lack renal function and lipid panel data. Blood pressure is 118/85 mmHg, heart rate 90 bpm. He is on six medications with moderate polypharmacy risk.

active_problems.name: Acute non‑ST segment elevation myocardial infarction
Microalbuminuria due to type 2 diabetes mellitus
Disorder of kidney due to diabetes mellitus

past_medical_history: The patient has a background of type 2 diabetes mellitus (diagnosed prior to 2016), chronic kidney disease stage 1 progressing to stage 2, prior episodes of stress, resolved gingivitis, resolved unhealthy alcohol drinking behavior, and a resolved acute viral pharyngitis in 2024. He has a history of multiple medication reviews and wellness visits. No documented mental health diagnoses are present, but psychosocial stressors have been noted.
